name: DigitalM Inside SEO
author: insideseo

sections.description:
DigitalM Inside SEO shows you the truth about your site, not a flattering “SEO score 85/100” but concrete facts and real errors.

Instead of a vanity score, Inside SEO explains problems in plain language: “84 people could not reach checkout, here is why and how to fix it.” Everything runs on your own site, and it reads the fields of your existing SEO plugin instead of replacing it.

Who it is for

  • WooCommerce stores that get traffic but not enough sales.
  • Service businesses that want to measure calls, emails and form submissions.
  • Blogs and content sites that want to know which content brings real results.

The Mirror, what search engines see

The home screen is one honest snapshot of your site: how many pages are indexable, which structured data types exist and which are missing, whether AI assistants can reach your content, and where titles, descriptions and H1s are missing or problematic. Numbers are measured from your real pages, not estimated.

Error audit, over 120 automated checks

The SEO screen runs more than 120 checks on your pages and groups the findings by priority, hardest first. The checks cover indexability (noindex, canonical and “discourage search engines” problems), content (thin text, missing alt text, near-duplicate or dead products, empty categories, heading problems), titles and meta (missing, too long, too short or duplicated), URL hygiene, internal links and orphaned pages, security headers, structured data, sitemap and robots, hreflang on multilingual sites, and hidden Cyrillic or mixed Latin/Cyrillic letters in SEO fields.

Each finding explains what it is, why it matters, where it is and how to fix it. You can fix titles and meta descriptions right there in the table, in bulk, and the check re-runs live so a fixed problem disappears on the spot.

Reviewed and accepted issues

Not every finding is a defect. On the findings that only a human can judge, you can mark one as reviewed with a reason (acceptable, client’s request, by design, not possible, postponed until a date, external cause, false alarm) and a short note. Accepted findings drop out of the count, the monthly plan and the site score, but stay in a separate “reviewed and clarified issues” table so nothing is hidden. A postponed one returns on its own after the date, and if the page is edited after you accepted it, the row is flagged for a fresh look.

Speed, from real visitors and your own server

Speed is measured three ways: Google PageSpeed Insights field data from the last 28 days, a lab test, and the plugin’s own load test that opens your pages and measures the server, the files, the plugins and the database queries. On top of the Google score it runs 31 of its own checks across server and WordPress, delivery, caching, fonts and plugins.

A standout is “what a plugin costs“: the plugin loads one of your pages with a single plugin’s files disabled, just for that request, and measures the difference, so you can see which plugin is actually slowing you down. You also get a page-weight breakdown by source, the slowest pages, a month-by-month history, a before/after view, and an optional comparison against up to three competitor URLs. All of it is free.

Optimization log

Every time you change a speed or file-loading rule, the plugin records it with the numbers from just before, and fills in the “after” numbers from the next test, so you can prove a change helped or undo it. You can add a manual note too, such as “switched host”.

Asset loading, which files load where

A per-page view of which CSS and JavaScript files load on which pages, so you can stop a plugin’s files from loading where that plugin is not used; one button clears all your shop’s files from the pages that have no shop on them. The plugin detects your cache plugin, gives you a ready exclusions list to copy into it, and warns you when another optimization plugin (Perfmatters, Asset CleanUp and similar) is already doing the same job.

Rankings

Connected to Google Search Console, the Rankings screen shows keyword and page positions, won and lost positions, and queries close to the top 10 so you can see quick wins. A rank tracker follows specific keywords day by day.

Duplicate content

Finds pages, products, categories and tags with near-identical text, the kind that makes Google unsure which one to rank. Each overlap is graded (over 70% red, 40-69% amber) and shows which other pages it collides with and by how much.

Spelling and proofreading

A real spell checker for your site content, built for Bulgarian and 19 other languages. It combines rule-based checks, a full LibreOffice dictionary (licences included, nothing sent to a third-party server) and grammar rules, and it never blocks a save, it only suggests. You keep a personal “my dictionary” so brand names are never flagged again, and product and category names are skipped automatically.

GEO / AEO, readiness for AI assistants

A dedicated screen checks whether AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and others) can reach your site, lists every AI bot with its robots.txt access, checks the structured data they understand, and shows the traffic and sales that already come from them. The plugin can also serve an llms.txt map of your key pages and products for AI crawlers, turned on or off from this screen.

Conversions and traffic (every site type)

The Conversions & Traffic screen works for every kind of site, not only stores. WooCommerce stores see orders by channel, revenue, a net-sales figure (minus VAT, shipping and refunds) and ROAS when you add an ad-spend file. Service sites and blogs see conversions as goals: calls, emails, form submissions, bookings and newsletter sign-ups. A Traffic sub-tab shows visitors, channels, devices, countries, cities and languages from GA4 for any site. Every figure is shown against the previous period of the same length.

Content planning

A Content view compares your existing articles against the topics your site should cover: it flags thin, cannibalizing or stale articles, finds topic gaps for new articles, and flags missing categories and tags, all read live from your own data.

Crawl

A full on-demand crawl of your own site detects broken links and orphaned pages, duplicated or broken canonicals and problematic filter URLs, and feeds the audit above, run as often as you like.

Change history

A change history records edits to titles, meta descriptions, alt text and file names, showing who made each change and when, and measures the effect three ways (30 days before vs after, month over month, and year over year) so you can see what actually moved.

Site guide and system information

A built-in Guide maps every feature to the tab it lives in and answers “where do I do X”. A System information screen shows your SEO plugin, cache plugin, site type, sitemap, tags, PHP and WordPress details in one place.

Removed pages and real 404s

When a page, product, post or category disappears, its address does not disappear from Google. The plugin keeps a list of removed addresses with what used to be there, what the address returns now, and how many clicks and impressions it had from Google. For each one you choose: redirect it to a related page, or mark it as gone for good (410). Real 404 hits are caught live.

Moving the site to a new address

The plugin remembers the address it works on. When the site moves (from staging to live, or to a new domain), it notices, pauses anything tied to the old address and asks you what to do, instead of mixing old and new data. A switch only to https or www is not treated as a move.

IndexNow (optional)

When you turn it on, the plugin notifies search engines that support IndexNow (Bing, Yandex and others) the moment you publish or update a page. It is off by default.

Working with an SEO agency (optional)

If an SEO agency looks after your site, it can send you an invitation link. The link opens a page on your own site that shows the agency’s name and exactly what it will be able to see and do. Nothing is shared until you confirm, and you can end the connection at any time from Settings → Agency. Every change the agency makes goes through a signed request and is written to a log on your site. Without an invitation, this part of the plugin does nothing.

Help and support

A built-in Guide answers “where do I do X” and takes you to the right screen. If something does not work, a form on the Guide screen sends us a short description together with the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, only when you press the button. If you leave the email from your account with us and tick the consent box, the message becomes a support ticket.

More of our plugins

A quiet page in the menu lists our other free plugins from the WordPress.org directory. Nothing is installed unless you press the Install button, which opens the standard WordPress installer.

Interface languages

The interface is available in Bulgarian and English. A BG/EN switch sits in the top right corner of every screen.

Everything above is free and fully functional, with no time limit and no locked features. An optional companion plugin from our own site adds AI-prepared suggestions and deeper analyses; this plugin works completely on its own without it.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or newer
  • PHP 8.1 or newer
  • WooCommerce (optional, for sales data)
  • Google Search Console and GA4 accounts for full data

External Services

DigitalM Inside SEO may communicate with the following external services when you use specific features.

seo.digitalmseo.com (our service)

  • What: the Google connection uses our service as a connection helper, so you do not have to create your own Google Cloud project.
  • When: only when you click “Connect Google account”.
  • What is sent: your site URL, plugin version, and a public verification key. Google tokens are stored only on your own site; our service never stores them.
  • Privacy Policy: https://seo.digitalmseo.com/en/privacy-policy/
  • Terms of Use: https://seo.digitalmseo.com/en/terms/

Google APIs (optional)

  • What: Search Console API and GA4 API.
  • When: when the user connects their accounts.
  • What is sent: OAuth tokens and data requests.
  • Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

seo.digitalmseo.com – SEO agency connection (optional)

  • What: our service checks agency invitations and passes approved requests between your site and the agency’s site.
  • When: only after you open an invitation link from an agency and confirm it. Nothing is sent before that.
  • What is sent: your site URL, plugin version and a public verification key. After you confirm, the agency’s site can read the SEO data shown on the consent page (findings, Google Search Console and GA4 history, rankings, the change log and daily visit figures) and send signed change requests, which are logged on your site. For the agency’s list of clients, our service may read a few summary numbers your site has already calculated and keep them for up to 15 minutes.
  • How to stop it: Settings → Agency → end the connection.

seo.digitalmseo.com – problem report form (optional)

  • What: the “Something not working?” form on the Guide screen.
  • When: only when you press the send button.
  • What is sent: your message, the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, the active SEO plugin, your site URL, and your email only if you tick the consent box.

Google PageSpeed Insights API (optional)

  • What: the speed test on the Speed screen.
  • When: when you run a speed test or schedule one.
  • What is sent: the public URL of the page being tested.
  • Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

IndexNow (optional, off by default)

  • What: api.indexnow.org, shared by Bing, Yandex and other search engines.
  • When: only after you turn it on, each time a page is published or updated.
  • What is sent: the public URL of the changed page and a key file address on your site.
  • Policy: https://www.indexnow.org/terms

WordPress.org plugin directory

  • What: the “More of our plugins” page reads the list of our plugins from the WordPress.org directory through the standard WordPress function.
  • When: when you open that page; the list is kept for 12 hours.
  • What is sent: the author name used for the search; nothing about your site.

AI provider APIs (optional)

  • What: AI suggestions for questions (FAQ) and schema on the GEO/AEO screen.
  • When: only when the user explicitly clicks a “Suggest” button, using the AI provider configured in WordPress Connectors or the user’s own API key.
  • What is sent: page context (title, content excerpt).
  • The user pays their AI provider directly; we never see or store the key on our servers.

Credits

Built by Digital M SEO Ltd (digitalmseo.com).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it directly from the WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Follow the setup wizard, or open Settings and connect Google Search Console and GA4.
  4. Run the first audit from the SEO screen.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free?

Yes. Everything in this plugin works forever with no time limit and no locked features.

What data do you collect and where do you store it?

The plugin collects data about the SEO health of your site (titles, meta descriptions, speed, rankings). This data is stored on your own WordPress site, not on our server.

Does it work with Yoast SEO, RankMath, SEOPress or All in One SEO?

Yes. Inside SEO is built to work alongside them, not to replace them. It reads the meta data from the active SEO plugin and adds deeper analysis.

Do I need Google Search Console and GA4?

Not strictly, but they are strongly recommended. Without them you will not see rankings, impressions, CTR and traffic data, only the technical checks.

Can an SEO agency manage my site through the plugin?

Only if you accept an invitation from that agency. You see what it will receive before you confirm, every change it makes is logged on your site, and you can end the connection at any time.

How do I report a problem?

Use the form at the bottom of the Guide screen. It is sent only when you press the button. Leave the email from your account with us to get the reply as a support ticket.

Does it support multilingual sites?

Yes. It runs hreflang checks automatically when it detects a multilingual setup.

Will the plugin slow down my site?

No. Scans run in small batches and never block a page load.

What is llms.txt?

It is a small map of your key pages and products for AI crawlers, served at yoursite.com/llms.txt. You can turn it on or off from the GEO/AEO screen.

Do you support AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini)?

Yes. The GEO/AEO screen checks whether AI bots can reach your site, whether you have structured data they understand, and whether your content is ready to be quoted.
sections.changelog:
0.294.94

  • Near-duplicates: the finding is called “Series of near-duplicate products” and counts series, as in the monthly audit. The make-unique list shows both: products and the series they are in.

0.294.93

  • The notices about the site check say “site crawl” (“The site crawl is running”, “stopped halfway”, “failed”), so they are not mixed up with the monthly audit.

0.294.92

  • Site check: a step that fails is tried again. Before, it was skipped quietly, the check finished without its data and whole kinds of findings disappeared (for example near-duplicate products).
  • System info: the Analytics channels row has its name.

0.294.91

  • System info: how much data comes from Google per day for the last 30 days (Search Console pages and queries, Analytics breakdowns), the limit, and on how many days the limit was reached. The agency sees the same numbers.

0.294.90

  • Agency link: writing, queue and commands from the agency need the agency’s signature, not only the link code. The agency’s public key comes from the hub. Until the key arrives, it works as before. A stolen link code can no longer write to the site.
  • Make unique list: “analyzed” also shows analyses made by the agency. New filter: with analysis, with proposal, with neither.

0.294.89

  • Site check: the link check works in short parts (about 20 seconds each). Before, a batch of slow links could run longer than the server allows, and the check stopped halfway.
  • Site check: if a step dies anyway, the check goes on by itself after about 6 minutes, without a manual restart.

0.294.88

  • Agency queue: the agency can now take series analysis tasks. When the agency analyzes a series, this site remembers it, so the rewrite can go to the queue.
  • Agency queue: the rewrite keeps its series and comes back for review as a full product, with image names and alt texts.
  • Agency queue: under an agency, “Run” and the night run hand the tasks to the agency. It takes them within about 30 minutes. The confirmation no longer shows this site’s credits and prices – the agency pays.
  • Agency queue: if the agency stops (no AI credits, limit), the task goes back to waiting instead of failing.

0.294.87

  • Make unique list: the column now shows how many products the series has (with the product itself), not how many others are similar.

0.294.86

  • Change log: paging with First, Back, a page number box, Next and Last. Paging and filters now keep working past the first page (the links had lost the read key).
  • Change log: new filter “Effect in Google” – improved, worse, no difference, waiting (under 30 days), no Google data.
  • Change log: shows how many rows it holds and about how much space. Full product texts are kept 90 days for undo, then shortened; rows are kept 24 months.

0.294.85

  • Audit: “Only one internal link” and “Broken internal links” moved to “Slowing down ranking”. The page is still seen; it just carries less weight.
  • Audit: 404 errors are now taken only from Google Search Console. The live 404 catcher also logs bots and old bookmarks, so it no longer counts in the audit.
  • Audit and index check: images, documents and theme or page-builder templates (for example Flatsome blocks under /blocks/) are no longer treated as pages, even when the sitemap lists them.

0.294.84

  • Spelling: each note is easier to read. The mistake is on the first line in red. Under it is the sentence where it stands, as a quote, with the mistake underlined. Then the type and the field in bold with the explanation, and last the fix in green with the buttons.
  • Spelling: the hint for “Fix by hand” is shown on its button again, not printed elsewhere on the page.

0.294.83

  • AI: the check whether the site’s AI provider works no longer sends a paid test request. It only asks WordPress whether a text model is set up. When a real request fails, the plugin remembers this for 10 minutes.

0.294.82

  • Audit: the questions before a fix are asked inside the page, with clear buttons (“Add to the queue”, “Replace everywhere”, “Fix”, “Move to draft”, “Delete for good” / “No”). No browser OK/Cancel window.
  • Change log: saving or removing questions and answers, the llms.txt choice, ad data and AI suggestions are now written to the change log.
  • Speed test (PageSpeed): works on sites without Action Scheduler. It uses WP-Cron when Action Scheduler is not there (for example, a site without WooCommerce). Before, the button said the test could not start.

0.294.81

  • Row writes cut long texts to the column size first, the same way the database did before. One long page title no longer stops a whole batch.
  • Uninstall runs in functions, deletes options through delete_option(), and also removes the plugin’s own term notes.

0.294.80

  • Database queries pass every value separately to the prepare step. Batch writes go row by row through the WordPress insert and replace helpers, inside one transaction.
  • Table upgrades use dbDelta only. No ALTER or DROP outside uninstall.

0.294.79

  • The plugin no longer defines WordPress core file-permission constants; file writes and copies give the permissions themselves.

0.294.78

  • llms.txt: page titles and descriptions are cleaned to plain text before they go into the file. The file is served as plain text with a no-sniff header.

0.294.77

  • New agency door for category and tag pages: create or find the term, write its text, meta text, featured image and attached products. Every step goes into the change log.
  • The agency can keep a suggested meta text next to a page, so the audit box keeps it.
  • The page material for the agency now includes the product price and code, and the full text for article review.
  • Missing English translations added.

0.294.76

  • The agency plugin can now read, save and remove the FAQ block and read the saved schema of a page, through the same signed and checked connection.
  • The agency view now includes the menu tree and the image renames that are still waiting.

0.294.75

  • Faster screens: reads from the plugin’s own tables go through the WordPress object cache. Any write to these tables clears it at once, so the screens always show the current data. With a persistent object cache (Redis, Memcached) the saving carries over between page loads.

0.294.74

  • Internal rename of two link and page list helpers (the old names still work). No visible change.

0.294.73

  • Speed, file rules: the “keep only on chosen pages” list for ordinary pages shows again.
  • A connected agency can read your page list for that choice.
  • The Google sign-in redirect uses wp_safe_redirect() with only the two Google addresses allowed.

0.294.72

  • Code review clean-up (screens work as before): no output buffering on the screens, a nonce on every admin screen address and GET filter form, a nonce on the front-end speed probe and file-rules preview addresses, the Google connection return finished through a form with a nonce.
  • The wp-config.php texts now say what really happens: the original is kept in memory, not copied to disk.

0.294.71

  • A connected agency can now save, on your site, what it sets for you: the file rules in Speed, the llms.txt selection, suggested questions and schema (they wait for approval as before), and your ads figures. Everything is written here and listed in the change log as before.
  • Fixed a PHP notice on the GEO/AEO screen.

0.294.70

  • New checks in the Errors tab: a past year in the text used as if it were the present; a title word that does not appear in the text; a page that is not in any menu.
  • A check for phone numbers and addresses written differently across pages is prepared but not switched on yet.

0.294.69

  • New checks in the Errors tab: title starting with a lowercase letter; double spaces and mixed quotes; address ending in “-2″/”-3″ when the same address without the number exists; product without a price or an image; image alt text equal to the product title; the same alt text on several images on one page; Cyrillic in an image file name; mixed alphabets in an image file name; image in the text without width and height.
  • Each new check has a help text, is counted as done from the change log where possible, and is checked again by “Check the changes”.

0.294.68

  • New: the connected agency can create a draft post on the site (title and a featured image from the site’s media library), add text to it in parts, and read its state. Only new drafts it created itself; nothing published is touched. Every step goes to the change log and can be undone (an undone draft goes to the trash, it is not deleted).
  • Fix: text sent by the agency keeps backslashes.

0.294.66

  • Fix: the “Run structure now” button (and the matching agency action) no longer fails.
  • Fix: speed “before/after” snapshots are saved again; the period column is widened on existing sites automatically.
  • Fix: the check for an incomplete upload now covers every plugin file.
  • Security: Google tokens, the site signing key, the PageSpeed key and the agency link code are also stored encrypted. Existing connections keep working; the old copies stay as a backup for this version.
  • Security: all agency endpoints use one shared check. Live actions and the queue accept only fresh requests and only from the remembered agency address. A new link forgets the old agency address.
  • Security: the hello endpoint gives environment and counts only over HTTPS, with an active link and consent. The hub summary also requires an active link.
  • Security: after a site address change, the hub summary pauses together with the agency endpoints until the owner decides.

0.294.65

  • Agency connection: the hourly status check sends the connection code, and a shorter answer from the hub no longer clears the agency contact details shown in the Agency tab.

0.294.64

  • Code review clean-up. Screens and data work as before.
  • SQL: every table and column name goes through the %i placeholder; IN lists and bulk inserts use placeholders; filters are fixed SQL with placeholders.
  • Input is sanitised where it is read; data from json_decode() is cleaned value by value.
  • Inline scripts and styles go through wp_add_inline_script() / wp_add_inline_style(); the consent page loads its CSS from a file.
  • File operations go through WP_Filesystem; wp-config.php is never copied to disk.
  • The HTTP/2 check no longer calls cURL directly.
  • Output buffers are closed in a finally block; every handler that changes data checks its nonce and capability itself.

0.294.63

  • The change log now keeps the full product title and both descriptions when the agency rewrites a product series, so the change can be undone from the log. The short description keeps its formatting when written by the agency.

0.294.62

  • The monthly GA4 breakdowns now also keep engaged sessions, average engagement time and key events, and add traffic source/medium and top products, so the full monthly report can be built from the stored data. No change in behaviour.

0.294.61

  • Housekeeping: cleared the remaining Plugin Check findings (removed a few no-op translation wrappers, tidied admin input handling, and annotated the internal database queries in the new data layers); softened the wording about the optional companion plugin, dropped a version-specific note, and show the name consistently as DigitalM Inside SEO. No change in behaviour.

0.294.57

  • New: removed pages list – every removed page, product, post or category with its Google clicks and impressions, ready to redirect or mark as gone (410); real 404 hits are caught live.
  • New: site move detection – when the site moves to a new address, the plugin pauses what is tied to the old one and asks what to do.
  • New: optional IndexNow notifications on publish and update (off by default).
  • New: optional connection with an SEO agency by invitation, with a consent page, a change log and a one-click disconnect.
  • New: “Something not working?” form on the Guide screen, sent only on click; with your account email and consent it becomes a support ticket.
  • New: a “More of our plugins” page that lists our other free plugins from WordPress.org; nothing is installed without your click.
  • Improved: over 120 error checks, clearer texts, full English interface, and all browser pop-up dialogs replaced with on-page messages.
  • Improved: a red warning when Google is connected but the last data download is more than two days old.

0.270.5

  • New: reviewed and accepted issues – mark a finding as reviewed with a reason and a note, so it drops out of the count, the plan and the score but stays in its own table; postponed ones return after their date.
  • New speed checks (main image lazy-loaded, oversized or old format; several oversized images; third-party fonts; missing font-display; missing preconnect; tracking before consent) and a new “external calls” server measurement.
  • New: an optimization log that records each speed and file-loading rule change with the before/after numbers, plus a per-page view of which CSS and JavaScript load where, cache-plugin detection and a warning when another optimization plugin is doing the same job.
  • Keyword impression counts now match Google Search Console exactly, and traffic figures are shown against the previous period.
  • Documentation: the readme now describes the above. This release also carries the earlier Plugin Check clean-up (file-level annotations on internal data-layer queries, recommended WordPress file functions, unslashed and sanitized admin inputs, a translators note) with the stable tag aligned to the version. No change in behaviour for the code-quality items.

0.267.10

  • English interface completed. The Spelling screen and its whole panel are now translated, along with a set of labels that were still showing in the source language: the database table names on the System information screen, the “Orders” metric, and the broken-install notice. Every interface string in the plugin and its scripts now has an English translation.

0.267.9

  • Plugin Check: the proofreading data layer now suppresses the direct-query warnings at file level (internal core tables, all values through prepare), clearing the last “incorrect number of replacements” warning on its post lookup.

0.267.8

  • Plugin Check: aligned the stable tag with the plugin version; the new proofreading and task-queue data layers now suppress the direct-query warnings at file level (internal tables, values passed through prepare); the proofreader AJAX handlers note that the nonce and capability are verified in their guard; and the queue on/off, URL and ID inputs are now unslashed and sanitized.

0.267.1

  • Money is no longer taken as proof that the meaning check succeeded – a truncated answer is paid for too. The flag travelling with the answer decides; the cost is only consulted when talking to a hub old enough not to send one. This is what was wiping grammar and style notes on a re-check.
  • A single-item check reports the real number of texts read instead of always saying one.

0.267.0

  • A re-check no longer erases what only the model can find. Grammar, meaning and style notes survive a pass in which the meaning check did not run – because it failed, was switched off, or the limit was gone – instead of being wiped by the dictionary-only result. They are dropped only when a real meaning pass replaces them.

0.266.99

  • The Fix button no longer appears on advice. A model answering a grammar note sometimes returns an instruction – “lower case for common nouns and finish the sentence” – rather than replacement text, and writing that into the page would destroy the sentence. A suggestion now earns its button only if it reads like a literal replacement: short enough, no brackets, quotes or “e.g.”, and sharing at least half its words with the text it replaces. Everything else says “fix by hand”.
  • The same test runs server-side, so an old page left open in a tab cannot push advice into the content either.

0.266.98

  • A run that was charged for is a run that happened. If the hub billed the request, the meaning check is reported as done even when the flag travelling with it says otherwise – which it could, when an older paid plugin passed the hub’s own “I handed this to the site” marker straight through.
  • When it really did not run, the line now names who was asked and how many texts were sent, so the reason is on screen instead of guessed.

For older versions, see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

The SEO screen runs more than 120 checks on your pages and groups the findings by priority, hardest first. The checks cover indexability (noindex, canonical and “discourage search engines” problems), content (thin text, missing alt text, near-duplicate or dead products, empty categories, heading problems), titles and meta (missing, too long, too short or duplicated), URL hygiene, internal links and orphaned pages, security headers, structured data, sitemap and robots, hreflang on multilingual sites, and hidden Cyrillic or mixed Latin/Cyrillic letters in SEO fields.

Each finding explains what it is, why it matters, where it is and how to fix it. You can fix titles and meta descriptions right there in the table, in bulk, and the check re-runs live so a fixed problem disappears on the spot.

Reviewed and accepted issues

Not every finding is a defect. On the findings that only a human can judge, you can mark one as reviewed with a reason (acceptable, client’s request, by design, not possible, postponed until a date, external cause, false alarm) and a short note. Accepted findings drop out of the count, the monthly plan and the site score, but stay in a separate “reviewed and clarified issues” table so nothing is hidden. A postponed one returns on its own after the date, and if the page is edited after you accepted it, the row is flagged for a fresh look.

Speed, from real visitors and your own server

Speed is measured three ways: Google PageSpeed Insights field data from the last 28 days, a lab test, and the plugin’s own load test that opens your pages and measures the server, the files, the plugins and the database queries. On top of the Google score it runs 31 of its own checks across server and WordPress, delivery, caching, fonts and plugins.

A standout is “what a plugin costs“: the plugin loads one of your pages with a single plugin’s files disabled, just for that request, and measures the difference, so you can see which plugin is actually slowing you down. You also get a page-weight breakdown by source, the slowest pages, a month-by-month history, a before/after view, and an optional comparison against up to three competitor URLs. All of it is free.

Optimization log

Every time you change a speed or file-loading rule, the plugin records it with the numbers from just before, and fills in the “after” numbers from the next test, so you can prove a change helped or undo it. You can add a manual note too, such as “switched host”.

Asset loading, which files load where

A per-page view of which CSS and JavaScript files load on which pages, so you can stop a plugin’s files from loading where that plugin is not used; one button clears all your shop’s files from the pages that have no shop on them. The plugin detects your cache plugin, gives you a ready exclusions list to copy into it, and warns you when another optimization plugin (Perfmatters, Asset CleanUp and similar) is already doing the same job.

Rankings

Connected to Google Search Console, the Rankings screen shows keyword and page positions, won and lost positions, and queries close to the top 10 so you can see quick wins. A rank tracker follows specific keywords day by day.

Duplicate content

Finds pages, products, categories and tags with near-identical text, the kind that makes Google unsure which one to rank. Each overlap is graded (over 70% red, 40-69% amber) and shows which other pages it collides with and by how much.

Spelling and proofreading

A real spell checker for your site content, built for Bulgarian and 19 other languages. It combines rule-based checks, a full LibreOffice dictionary (licences included, nothing sent to a third-party server) and grammar rules, and it never blocks a save, it only suggests. You keep a personal “my dictionary” so brand names are never flagged again, and product and category names are skipped automatically.

GEO / AEO, readiness for AI assistants

A dedicated screen checks whether AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and others) can reach your site, lists every AI bot with its robots.txt access, checks the structured data they understand, and shows the traffic and sales that already come from them. The plugin can also serve an llms.txt map of your key pages and products for AI crawlers, turned on or off from this screen.

Conversions and traffic (every site type)

The Conversions & Traffic screen works for every kind of site, not only stores. WooCommerce stores see orders by channel, revenue, a net-sales figure (minus VAT, shipping and refunds) and ROAS when you add an ad-spend file. Service sites and blogs see conversions as goals: calls, emails, form submissions, bookings and newsletter sign-ups. A Traffic sub-tab shows visitors, channels, devices, countries, cities and languages from GA4 for any site. Every figure is shown against the previous period of the same length.

Content planning

A Content view compares your existing articles against the topics your site should cover: it flags thin, cannibalizing or stale articles, finds topic gaps for new articles, and flags missing categories and tags, all read live from your own data.

Crawl

A full on-demand crawl of your own site detects broken links and orphaned pages, duplicated or broken canonicals and problematic filter URLs, and feeds the audit above, run as often as you like.

Change history

A change history records edits to titles, meta descriptions, alt text and file names, showing who made each change and when, and measures the effect three ways (30 days before vs after, month over month, and year over year) so you can see what actually moved.

Site guide and system information

A built-in Guide maps every feature to the tab it lives in and answers “where do I do X”. A System information screen shows your SEO plugin, cache plugin, site type, sitemap, tags, PHP and WordPress details in one place.

Removed pages and real 404s

When a page, product, post or category disappears, its address does not disappear from Google. The plugin keeps a list of removed addresses with what used to be there, what the address returns now, and how many clicks and impressions it had from Google. For each one you choose: redirect it to a related page, or mark it as gone for good (410). Real 404 hits are caught live.

Moving the site to a new address

The plugin remembers the address it works on. When the site moves (from staging to live, or to a new domain), it notices, pauses anything tied to the old address and asks you what to do, instead of mixing old and new data. A switch only to https or www is not treated as a move.

IndexNow (optional)

When you turn it on, the plugin notifies search engines that support IndexNow (Bing, Yandex and others) the moment you publish or update a page. It is off by default.

Working with an SEO agency (optional)

If an SEO agency looks after your site, it can send you an invitation link. The link opens a page on your own site that shows the agency’s name and exactly what it will be able to see and do. Nothing is shared until you confirm, and you can end the connection at any time from Settings → Agency. Every change the agency makes goes through a signed request and is written to a log on your site. Without an invitation, this part of the plugin does nothing.

Help and support

A built-in Guide answers “where do I do X” and takes you to the right screen. If something does not work, a form on the Guide screen sends us a short description together with the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, only when you press the button. If you leave the email from your account with us and tick the consent box, the message becomes a support ticket.

More of our plugins

A quiet page in the menu lists our other free plugins from the WordPress.org directory. Nothing is installed unless you press the Install button, which opens the standard WordPress installer.

Interface languages

The interface is available in Bulgarian and English. A BG/EN switch sits in the top right corner of every screen.

Everything above is free and fully functional, with no time limit and no locked features. An optional companion plugin from our own site adds AI-prepared suggestions and deeper analyses; this plugin works completely on its own without it.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or newer
  • PHP 8.1 or newer
  • WooCommerce (optional, for sales data)
  • Google Search Console and GA4 accounts for full data

External Services

DigitalM Inside SEO may communicate with the following external services when you use specific features.

seo.digitalmseo.com (our service)

  • What: the Google connection uses our service as a connection helper, so you do not have to create your own Google Cloud project.
  • When: only when you click “Connect Google account”.
  • What is sent: your site URL, plugin version, and a public verification key. Google tokens are stored only on your own site; our service never stores them.
  • Privacy Policy: https://seo.digitalmseo.com/en/privacy-policy/
  • Terms of Use: https://seo.digitalmseo.com/en/terms/

Google APIs (optional)

  • What: Search Console API and GA4 API.
  • When: when the user connects their accounts.
  • What is sent: OAuth tokens and data requests.
  • Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

seo.digitalmseo.com – SEO agency connection (optional)

  • What: our service checks agency invitations and passes approved requests between your site and the agency’s site.
  • When: only after you open an invitation link from an agency and confirm it. Nothing is sent before that.
  • What is sent: your site URL, plugin version and a public verification key. After you confirm, the agency’s site can read the SEO data shown on the consent page (findings, Google Search Console and GA4 history, rankings, the change log and daily visit figures) and send signed change requests, which are logged on your site. For the agency’s list of clients, our service may read a few summary numbers your site has already calculated and keep them for up to 15 minutes.
  • How to stop it: Settings → Agency → end the connection.

seo.digitalmseo.com – problem report form (optional)

  • What: the “Something not working?” form on the Guide screen.
  • When: only when you press the send button.
  • What is sent: your message, the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, the active SEO plugin, your site URL, and your email only if you tick the consent box.

Google PageSpeed Insights API (optional)

  • What: the speed test on the Speed screen.
  • When: when you run a speed test or schedule one.
  • What is sent: the public URL of the page being tested.
  • Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

IndexNow (optional, off by default)

  • What: api.indexnow.org, shared by Bing, Yandex and other search engines.
  • When: only after you turn it on, each time a page is published or updated.
  • What is sent: the public URL of the changed page and a key file address on your site.
  • Policy: https://www.indexnow.org/terms

WordPress.org plugin directory

  • What: the “More of our plugins” page reads the list of our plugins from the WordPress.org directory through the standard WordPress function.
  • When: when you open that page; the list is kept for 12 hours.
  • What is sent: the author name used for the search; nothing about your site.

AI provider APIs (optional)

  • What: AI suggestions for questions (FAQ) and schema on the GEO/AEO screen.
  • When: only when the user explicitly clicks a “Suggest” button, using the AI provider configured in WordPress Connectors or the user’s own API key.
  • What is sent: page context (title, content excerpt).
  • The user pays their AI provider directly; we never see or store the key on our servers.
